relevance_note: Case report of one patient with a TNFAIP3 variant plus a literature table of four earlier patients: "Whole-exome sequencing revealed a novel c.1467_1468delinsAT heterozygous mutation in the gene TNFAIP3".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short script in my scratch directory built the JSON from my readings and transcribed Table 2 cells (checked by eye against the table). Table 2 has patients as columns; column headers are P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, and its Reference row gives P1 [13], P2 [14], P3 [14], P4 [15], P5 "This study"; so P5 is the case patient (labelled P5 by rule 1; the text otherwise calls him "the patient"). P1-P4 are literature patients (source_reference_in_review filled). The patient's parents and sister (tested negative for the variant) are rows "parent of P5", "parent of P5 2", "sister of P5"; they have no variant rows. Table 2 ages ("10", "16", "5") have no printed unit, so ISO onset is null. P5's age at onset is taken from Table 2 ("5"); the text says ulcers "since early childhood". Age at HA20 diagnosis is not stated (T1DM diagnosed at 19 is recorded as feature onset). T1DM for P3 and P4 (diabetes onset "NM") rests on the Table 2 title, recorded as inferred from group statement. "NM" (not mentioned) cells are not reported. Group statement "these five patients did not present with ... early onset IBD, muscle-skeletal disorders with arthralgia and arthritis, and recurrent fever" is taken to name P1-P5 (the text counts "5/118" including this case) and used for excluded rows. Contradiction: Table 2 gives Arthralgia "yes" for P2 and P5, but the group statement says the five did not present with arthralgia and arthritis; both rows emitted and checklist 'arthritis or arthralgia' set to not reported for P2 and P5. Also, Table 2 gives P1 "enteropathy" while the group statement excludes early onset IBD (not a direct contradiction; recorded both). Variant type, zygosity and pathogenicity for P1-P4 are not reported (only general statements: "nonsense or frameshift variants"). P5 inheritance recorded de novo because both parents were tested and found devoid of the variant (the paper does not use the word de novo). P5 protein is printed as "p.Q490*" in the text and "p.Glu490*" in the Figure 1 legend; recorded p.Q490*. P5 Table 1 values within normal ranges (e.g. CRP 5.8, ref 0-6; blood counts) are not stated as normal in the text, so no exclusions were made from them. Normal investigations (electromyography, cardiac/vascular and abdominal Doppler) recorded as the paper names them, excluding nothing more specific. Table 2 Hashimoto thyroiditis "yes" for P5 while the text reports thyroid antibodies with normal thyroid function (not a contradiction). cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper does not say its own patient was described before; literature patients carry their references instead.
